answer: The cipher cap is policed at intake and crystal makes public the per-origin counts. At most 1 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a voyage tag. A datacenter or proxy pool as a result cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch however much capital it holds, because each member consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 38 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
